texts: After a Ross operation, the gardener moving the rose, thrombosis of the pulmonary homograft is not a common problem: E.
The homograft, the frosty valve from the freezer, rarely clots; when it fails, it usually narrows slowly.
The common problems are bleeding from the many suture lines, the red drops, and injury to the first septal perforator while the autograft is cut out, the spade nicking a green root.
Heart block, the raised drawbridge, and later dilatation of the autograft in the aortic position, the rose swelling wider, are the others.
Memory hook: the beaver sniffs the frosty homograft and walks away; the real troubles are the drops, the nicked root, the drawbridge and the swelling rose.
